Area.evidence_source: [/page/14/Text/15] Over half the prisoners (27/46, 59%) said that they chose not to tell anyone outside prison about their attempted suicide. This was usually because there was either no one to tell or they did not want to upset or worry their family: [/page/15/Text/3] I try and keep it as quiet as possible cause I don't want to get bullied ... people will think you can't cope or something. (Case 1) [/page/15/Text/9] Conversely, some prisoners also expressed a desire to attempt suicide again: [/page/15/Text/10] It [the suicide attempt] don't affect me. I'd do it again. I'd say give me a gun now and I'll blow me head off. That's it. (Case 23) [/page/14/Text/17] When prisoners' families and friends did find out about the suicide attempt, prisoners said that the predominant reaction was one of upset or concern for the prisoner. Similarly, prisoners said that the reactions they faced from inside the prison following a suicide attempt were largely positive. Most prisoners felt that they were treated better, 'OK' or no differently by staff. [/page/15/Text/7] Another common feeling was that the suicide attempt had made the prisoner feel better than before the act: [/page/15/Text/8] It was a slap round the face with reality. It made me feel much better. I've had a think about things and realised that I am a silly little arse and that there is more than just my feelings. (Case 28)
